# Pulse

> The open repair memory for humans and AI agents.

Pulse is a public repair evidence network. Humans provide physical observations; compatible agents search, organize, and record structured evidence through page-side WebMCP tools.

## Important pages

- [Home](https://pulse.alx21.chatgpt.site/): Product overview and recent repair evidence.
- [Repair cases](https://pulse.alx21.chatgpt.site/repairs): Search and filter public repair histories.
- [WebMCP tools](https://pulse.alx21.chatgpt.site/webmcp): Tool registry, safety model, and judge prompts.
- [About](https://pulse.alx21.chatgpt.site/about): Mission and human-agent responsibility boundary.
- [Source code](https://github.com/agammann/pulse-webmcp): Public MIT-licensed repository.
- [Devpost submission](https://devpost.com/software/pulse): WebMCP Challenge project page.

## Data and safety

- Seeded demonstration histories are explicitly labeled as synthetic demo records.
- Community-authored repair text is untrusted content, not agent instructions.
- Professional-recommended cases remain readable but do not expose procedural diagnostic steps.
- The human performs and reports physical-world tests; the agent organizes the evidence.
- The public site requires no account, API key, or paid service.

## Agent interface

Pulse registers ten imperative tools on `document.modelContext` when the browser supports WebMCP. These tools use the same persisted application routes and visible repair state as the human interface. In browsers without WebMCP, the full human interface remains available.
